properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26, in his own words: *"could we create a very dynamic and fluid node that has edges to other nodes in the graph that a user asks something to be done or the agent identifies that something needs to be addressed. once a task is dealt with, the edge to that the hotspot node could be deleted?... the task node then almost becomes a scratchpad of what needs to be done and once something is done, it is removed from the node text field (aka scratchpad) because the node isn't designed as an enduring record (that's what git commit history and changelog files are for). mostly just thinking about how the agent can start using the graph itself."*

**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.**

═══ 🛑 SCOPE — CORRECTED BY ANTHONY THE SAME DAY, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE HERE ═══

*"just a quick note, the task node wasn't strictly for reflow2's own purposes. it is for every reflow2 project and any agent (Claude, grok, openai, etc). I just want to reiterate that."*

**THIS IS A PRODUCT QUESTION, NOT A SELF-HOSTING ONE.** The first draft of this node reasoned almost entirely from reflow2's own repository — its handoff hook, its detectors, its claims. That is the pull `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` exists to resist, and he has now stated the general form three separate times. The self-hosting evidence stays because it is real evidence, but it is a WITNESS rather than the SUBJECT.

⭐⭐ **AND THE CORRECTION MAKES HIS ORIGINAL ARGUMENT MUCH STRONGER THAN THE VERSION FIRST RECORDED.** He argued a markdown handoff is not transportable ACROSS MACHINES. The sharper fact is that it is not transportable ACROSS AGENTS: `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/` is Claude Code furniture. **A grok, OpenAI or Codex agent working the same design has no such directory, no such file, and no way to read one.** So the pattern does not merely degrade on a second laptop — it is unavailable to most of reflow2's intended users on day one.

⭐ **THE CONSEQUENCE THAT FOLLOWS, AND IT ARGUES FOR THE IDEA:** the design graph is the ONLY thing every agent working a project shares. Not the harness, not the memory store, not the hooks, not the slash commands. `dec:skills-served` already made this argument for skills — served from the server so they match the running version and nothing in the repo goes stale — and a working set is the same shape of problem. **Whatever carries "what needs doing" has to live where every agent can reach it, and the graph is the only candidate.** That is a far better reason to build this than anything in the first draft.

⚠️ **A WARNING THIS OPENS, WHICH BELONGS WITH `dec:idea-where-does-tool-use-actually-fail-four-layers`:** reflow2's mechanisms for making an agent USE it are themselves Claude-Code-shaped — Stop and PostToolUse hooks, `.claude/settings.json`, 23 slash commands. Those reach one harness. The MCP tool surface reaches all of them. **So the layer-② trigger work measured so far may be less portable than the layer-③ and layer-④ work, and nobody has stated that.**

═══ WHAT IS ACTUALLY BEING PROPOSED, and it is sharper than a to-do list ═══

Not a Task type. A single node whose **edges ARE the worklist** — draw one at a node needing attention, delete it when dealt with — and whose **text is a scratchpad that shrinks as work completes**. Explicitly *not* an enduring record, on the stated ground that git history and the changelog already are.

⭐ **THE INVERSION THAT MAKES IT INTERESTING.** Everything else in a reflow2 graph is built to endure. `retire-from-design` forces one question before anything leaves — *"was this ever true?"* — because history is retired on the record while a mistake is deleted, and confusing the two either erases the past or embalms a typo. `OBSOLETES` exists so a withdrawal has an author. `Snapshot`, `DesignEpoch` and `ChangeEvent` all exist to stop things vanishing. **A node designed to be erased would be the first construct to deliberately opt out**, and the question is whether that discipline leaks once one exists.

═══ THERE IS ALREADY A PRECEDENT, AND IT WORKS ═══

**Claims.** `claim_region` draws an advisory marker whose liveness is COMPUTED rather than stored; `release_claim` deletes it and leaves nothing behind. Exercised on reflow2's own design 2026-08-26 — drawn and released, no history lost because none was owed. **So an ephemeral construct already exists in the product and nobody argues it corrupts anything.** That is the strongest evidence for the hotspot being admissible in principle, and it generalises to any project because claims are a shipped feature rather than a local habit.

═══ THE OBJECTION THAT MATTERS MOST ═══

🛑 **Deleting an edge cannot say whether the work was DONE or ABANDONED**, and those are the two states `retire-from-design` exists to keep apart. A worklist that forgets which is which will, over months, lose the record of things decided against — and *"we considered that and dropped it"* is exactly the memory this project keeps saying is worth more than the thing itself.

⭐ A possible answer, untested: a real completion writes a ChangeEvent, so **an edge deleted with no ChangeEvent in the window IS the abandoned case, computably.** That would make the distinction derivable rather than stored — the same move `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` already makes.

═══ THE SPLIT THAT DECIDES HOW MUCH IS NEEDED ═══

- **COMPUTABLE** — open gaps, failing checks, drift awaiting disposition, capabilities claiming built with no check, answers never written back. `loop_status` computes ALL of it today in one cheap call, for any project. **A hotspot holding these would duplicate a computation and immediately risk disagreeing with it.**
- **EXOGENOUS** — *"Jakub said finish the tests"* (his own words, from NSLS-II rather than from reflow2), *"the vendor confirmed the API changes in March"*, *"CI was pending when I stopped"*. Facts about the world, underivable from any design. **This half has no home in any reflow2 project**, and is what `dec:idea-is-there-a-lightweight-task-capture-below-the-increment-grain` opened on 2026-08-25 — also from real work rather than from reflow2's own development.

So the hotspot may be far smaller than it first looks: a home for the exogenous half, with the computable half left where it already lives and never mirrored.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) One hotspot node per design, edges as worklist, text as scratchpad.** As proposed. ⚠️ Counter, and it is specific rather than aesthetic: a single node accumulating edges from everywhere becomes a **hub that distorts the structural detectors** — betweenness, community detection, articulation points and `surprising_connections` all reason about connectivity, and they would read a scratchpad as topology. **This hits every consumer's design, not just reflow2's** — any project running `detect_defects` would start seeing its own to-do list reported as a god-node or a sole bridge.

**(b) Exogenous items only, as small nodes, with the worklist COMPUTED as "these plus what loop_status owes."** Avoids the hub problem and the duplication. ⚠️ Counter: close to option C of the 2026-08-25 task question and inherits its objection — a translation step at the moment the user wants to dump three sentences and move on.

**(c) Do not store it at all; make the working set a projection, like orientation.** Most consistent with `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written`. ⚠️ Counter: cannot hold the exogenous half by construction, and that is the half worth carrying.

**(d) Keep the scratchpad OUT of a text field, whatever else is decided.** A prose field edited by successive sessions has no merge story, and reflow2 is explicitly multi-writer through a shared server — and now explicitly multi-AGENT. Two sessions erasing different lines of one scratchpad is a lost update with no conflict, exactly what `expected_content_hash` was added to prevent, and it would not even be detected. **With several different agents on one design this stops being a corner case.**

📌 His closing framing, now read in the corrected scope: *"mostly just thinking about how the agent can start using the graph itself."* Not *this* agent, and not on *this* project — **any agent, on any design, reaching for the one thing they all share.**
properties.name: OPEN — can a design brain hold a deliberately EPHEMERAL node, whose edges are the live worklist and whose text is erased as work completes?
properties.rationale:
Judged distinct from the handoff question after reading it: that one is about a contradiction in the repository and could be closed by deleting a hook; this is about whether an ephemeral construct belongs in a graph built to endure, which survives that answer either way.

The claims precedent is recorded because it settles the in-principle objection with evidence rather than argument — an ephemeral, computed, deletable marker already exists here and has caused no harm. What remains is not "may we?" but "what shape, and which half of the worklist".

The hub objection sits at option level rather than as a verdict because it is a specific structural consequence — this design's own algorithms would read the node as topology — and it is the kind of thing that is obvious afterwards and expensive to discover after building.
